tpoacher · Nov 28, 2026

Technically, it's not "the devil" in the Christian sense (or any other religion that believes in the devil) per se.

The setting is an alternate universe / cosmology where there exist forces of good and forces of evil of a very particular nature and history, and where such forces are entirely mortal and occupying physical realms (albeit generally unreachable by ordinary humans / your average Jo).

Obviously the terminology borrows heavily from Christian (and not only) vocabulary for familiarity and effect, but has little to do with current religious beliefs in principle.

In this universe, Diablo is simply one of the higher-ranked "generals" in the "forces of evil"; but is not particularly special either, and there are others like him (e.g. Baal, and Mephisto, as well as the slightly lower ranked Azmodan, Belial, Andariel, and Duriel).

And similarly Tyrael and others are generals on the other side ("the council of angels of the High Heavens"), which purports itself to be "the good side", but, all is relative, of course.

So in some sense, Diablo is closer to Starwars and the Jedi vs Sith wars, than it is to Christianity, except for the fact that it is heavily sprinkled with "biblical" vocabulary.

WhereIsTheTruth · Nov 28, 2026

Modern action RPGs took all the wrong lessons from Diablo 2

It was never about the mindless hack'n'slash, it was about everything surrounding it, from the exploration, the atmosphere, the character building, all the thrill of discovery, and the sense of adventuring into hostile, dark and mysterious world

Combat was a means to experience that world, it was never excuse to turn it into a slot machine with explosion everywhere (i'm looking at you Path of Exile, even you, modern Blizzard)

Even David Brevik, the father of Diablo, is not very happy with what the genre has become [1]

Very few AAA studios managed to recapture that feeling, FromSoftware is one of them, with Demon Souls and Dark Souls series

I don't think we'll ever experience a game like Diablo 2 again, and i don't think Blizzard can ever manage to undo the harm D3 & D4 have done to this IP

[1] https://www.videogamer.com/features/diablo-creator-david-bre...

I never played Diablo 2 much, but I got deeply into Diablo 3 with friends from work. Obviously a different game, but what I found most enjoyable about that one is that, at the highest levels of difficulty, it transforms into playing something like Doom.

In Doom, both you and your enemy are highly lethal to one another. I describe it as being like two scorpions fighting one another; both have essentially one-touch lethality against one another. You survive by constantly moving, weaving in and out of opponents and deftly swapping weapons as needed.

Diablo 3 at very high difficulties with high-level builds is the same. Playing successfully really emphasizes the action element of ARPG. It’s far from mindless, and can actually require a lot of concentration.

Did the highest levels of difficulty in Diablo 2 demand that kind of precision and skilled play, in both build and combat?
